Undergraduate Admissions

Your Path to Minerva

A selective, holistic admissions process paired with a clear and transparent approach to cost and financial support.

Minerva’s admissions process is designed to understand how you think, approach challenges, and engage with ideas.

At the same time, we believe you should have a clear understanding of cost and financial support early in your decision-making process.

Who Can Apply

To apply to Minerva’s undergraduate program, you must:

01

Be completing or have completed secondary school

02

Be prepared to enroll in a full-time, four-year degree program

03

Demonstrate proficiency in English

Minerva welcomes applicants from all countries and backgrounds and provides support and guidance on visas and relocation across global cities.

A Holistic Approach

Minerva takes a holistic approach to admissions, focused on your potential, perspective, and ability to be a global leader solving complex problems.

We consider:

Intellectual potential and analytical thinking

Curiosity, initiative, and motivation

Creativity, leadership, and community impact

Your ability to collaborate in a global learning environment


Standardized tests are not required. Instead, the process is designed to understand how you approach problems and ideas.

Application Rounds

Minerva offers multiple application rounds throughout the admissions cycle, including Early Decision and Regular Decision.

Early Action (Binding Optional)

The Early Action cycle at Minerva offers students the flexibility of both binding and non-binding admissions options. Students who are certain Minerva is their first choice may choose binding admission. If admitted, binding students will be required to enroll within 10 days of receiving their admissions decision.

Regular Decision

Regular Decision is non-binding and allows you to compare offers before making a final decision.


Deadlines and decision timelines vary by cycle.

What to Expect

Applying to Minerva is an opportunity to demonstrate how you think and is designed to understand your reasoning, experiences, and potential.

Step 1

Submit your application

Provide your background, academic history, and personal information.

Step 2

Complete assessments and challenges

After submitting, you’ll complete a set of interactive challenges designed to evaluate how you think.


These include:

  • Short exercises in reasoning, problem-solving, and communication
  • Tasks that assess creativity and analytical thinking


These challenges are timed and structured, but require no prior preparation.

Step 3

Share your accomplishments

Highlight the work, projects, and experiences that matter most to you.

You’ll have the opportunity to:

  • Provide examples of your impact and achievements
  • Add context about your role and what you learned
  • Submit supporting materials if relevant

Tips for success

Focus on your thinking process, not “right answers”

Be specific about your contributions and impact

Use clear examples rather than general statements

Complete the challenges in a focused, distraction-free environment

Start Your Application

Starting Your Application

You can start your application through the Common Application or directly on our website. We recommend applying directly through Minerva for the most seamless experience.

Part 1 collects your biographical and academic information. Applicants under 18 will also provide a parent or guardian's contact details.

Once submitted, you'll move on to the Minerva Challenges, a unique, interactive set of online tasks that measure your reasoning, creativity, and communication skills.

Before You Begin

Use a reliable desktop or laptop computer with a stable internet connection.

Complete your application in a quiet, comfortable environment where you can focus without interruptions.

You can save your progress and return to your application at any time. You do not need to complete everything in one sitting.

How You Think

Instead of standardized test scores, Minerva uses online challenges to evaluate how you think.

You do not need to prepare for these challenges. Some include brief practice sessions to help you get comfortable with the format.

Math, Reasoning, Comprehension & Thinking

Timed challenges in:

Math

Logical Reasoning

Reading Comprehension

Divergent Thinking

Approximate time: 8–20 minutes each

Written & Verbal Communication Tasks

Written and verbal communication tasks that explore your perspectives and experiences.

Approximate time: 20 minutes each

Tips for Success
  • Take the challenges when you're alert and focused.
  • Read all instructions carefully.
  • Work in a quiet, uninterrupted space.
  • Trust your instincts. We're evaluating your approach, not perfection.
  • Be authentic. Respond naturally, not rehearsed.
  • Remember that each challenge measures a different kind of thinking. Variety is a strength.
  • Check your tech setup before you begin. A desktop or laptop is required (no tablets or phones).
  • Close other programs to prevent lag during timed portions.
  • Keep a notepad nearby for jotting down quick ideas.

What You've Done

We don't define achievement for you. You get to show us what matters most.

You'll describe your achievements and provide supporting materials such as documents, links, or references.

Your accomplishments can include:

Personal projects or creative work

Academic competitions or artistic pursuits

Leadership roles

Community involvement

Work experience

Guidance for Presenting Your Accomplishments
  • Include context by explaining what inspired the project and your specific role.
  • Show outcomes by describing the impact of your work or what you learned.
  • Upload clear documentation or links, such as portfolios, videos, or reports.
  • Highlight depth and authenticity over quantity.

Your Academic Background

Our admissions committee reviews your academic history to evaluate your readiness and ensure you are well prepared to succeed in Minerva's active, discussion-based learning environment.

You'll need to provide:

Your most recent three years of academic records, which may include transcripts from multiple institutions.

Verification from a school counselor or equivalent official.

More About Transcripts & Requirements

Our admissions committee reviews your academic trajectory, course rigor, and consistency, not just your grades.

  • Submit transcripts covering your most recent three years of coursework, including any dual-enrollment, IB, AP, A-Level, or other international programs, if applicable.
  • Official transcripts should be sent directly by your school counselor, registrar, or other authorized school official.
  • If you order transcripts through your school, Parchment, Scoir, or another transcript service, have them sent to admissions@minerva.edu. A school official must still complete the required academic form.
  • If your transcripts are not in English, you may be asked to provide certified translations.
  • Additional documentation may be requested depending on your educational background or country-specific requirements.

Minerva values how you've challenged yourself academically and your readiness for active, discussion-based learning.

Binding Admission

Minerva offers a binding admission option in the Early Action cycle for applicants who are confident Minerva is their first choice. If admitted through the binding option, you are required to enroll and withdraw applications to other institutions within 10 days of receiving your admissions decision.

Early Decision is best suited for students who:

Have fully explored Minerva’s model

Are ready to commit to a four-year, global undergraduate experience

Transfer to Minerva

Designed for students who have completed at least one year of university coursework and are seeking a more rigorous, global, and interdisciplinary education.

Eligible students may apply prior coursework toward a Minerva degree and complete their studies in three years, while fully participating in Minerva’s global and immersive learning model.

How it Works

Transfer up to 32 credits (approximately one academic year)

Begin major coursework earlier while maintaining interdisciplinary breadth

Follow a structured, advisor-supported three-year degree plan

Participate fully in global rotations, applied learning, and civic engagement

Who it's For

Students currently enrolled at another university

Students who have completed one year or more of full-time coursework

Students seeking an accelerated, global, and applied learning experience

Questions about transferring? Contact: admissions@minerva.edu.

Application Policies

To ensure a fair and consistent process:

You may submit only one application per admissions year

Applications cannot be transferred between programs

If you are not admitted, you may reapply in a future year

Financial Aid Timing

Students who wish to be considered for financial aid must submit required financial documentation as part of the application process.

Financial aid decisions are released alongside admissions decisions.

Applying early is recommended, as funding is limited.
